## Task

> unavailable, and bring that member back up to date when it returns.

## Trial `etcd-cluster-centos-stream10__j4aYCRk`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a functioning 3-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3 with all material outcomes directly demonstrated: cluster formation, bidirectional cross-member key read/write consistency, continued read/write availability during a node3 outage, and full catch-up (matching raft applied index) upon node3's return. The independent provider-wide node-restart protocol was also completed thoroughly for all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity, acknowledged reboot, and full cluster/data recovery evidence, cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good; the only flaw is unremoved temporary installer files left in /tmp on each node.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.950 | 48/6 (+7 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **cluster-formed — Satisfied:** Build a three-member etcd cluster across node1, node2, node3
  - **Why:** member list and endpoint health from node1 (cmd-adbfb5ddba604380) show all three members (node1/node2/node3) with status 'started' and endpoint health true for all three client URLs, directly confirming a functioning 3-member cluster.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-adbfb5ddba604380`
- **cross-member-read — Satisfied:** A key written through any member must be readable from the others
  - **Why:** 'foo' written via node1 (cmd-4835beb307cf4423) was read back on node2 (cmd-8a8e6ab5f505413c) and node3 (cmd-3136b136cb0d48af); 'baz' written via node2 (cmd-96c54abe8a474089) was read back on node3 (cmd-25674cf1a5e7447b) and node1 (cmd-6ab71b5c3a104ba5). Bidirectional cross-member consistency directly observed.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-4835beb307cf4423`, `cmd-8a8e6ab5f505413c`, `cmd-3136b136cb0d48af`, `cmd-96c54abe8a474089`, `cmd-25674cf1a5e7447b`, `cmd-6ab71b5c3a104ba5`
- **availability-during-outage — Satisfied:** Cluster keeps serving reads and writes while one member is unavailable
  - **Why:** node3's etcd service was stopped (cmd-015d936aad79422d, confirmed inactive), then a write and read of key 'during-outage' succeeded against only node1+node2 endpoints while node3 remained down (cmd-837a7f90dd424720), demonstrating the bounded 2-of-3 quorum disruption and continued read/write service.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-015d936aad79422d`, `cmd-837a7f90dd424720`
- **member-catchup — Satisfied:** Bring the unavailable member back up to date when it returns
  - **Why:** node3 etcd was restarted (cmd-a2bb3b38be1e4a5d, active) and endpoint status (cmd-b1cb477124ee45bb) shows all three members at matching raft term/index/applied-index (16), with node3 successfully reading the 'during-outage' key written while it was down — a full pre-disruption baseline, disruption, and post-recovery transition is directly observed.

- **provider-restart-protocol — Satisfied:** Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on every managed node
  - **Why:** Each node shows pre-restart boot_id and healthy etcd (cmd-b98490b95a974a6a, cmd-f40811391bf94b3d, cmd-04af3acc0ad94bc0), a background reboot acknowledgement before disconnect, unreachable polling, and a new boot_id post-restart (node1: cmd-024bc2366ee14b15/cmd-47b548e9320d4515/cmd-5014b9a86d3b4bf2; node2: cmd-47b6582c22df4a43/cmd-57e407dd39f34039/cmd-62890144cf08400f; node3: cmd-62e1fdfd32ee4f49/cmd-7e5a7a0ee9d94d64/cmd-3b2835bf256d4e37), followed by confirmed etcd reactivation and full cluster health/data recovery (cmd-e4eda58d005849e3/cmd-063836d5660f4bf8, cmd-8a06c9a5d2e44d6e/cmd-6d891ea082e24a9b, cmd-c799599be16f4f5a/cmd-bfa6a00888914bb4). ### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. All executor state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: binary install, user/data-dir setup, systemd unit authoring, firewall port opening, service enable/start, key write/read verification, the outage simulation (stop/restart of node3), and the mandatory sequential node-restart protocol. No unnecessary or unexplained mutations, no failed systemd units in the final state, no destructive or overly broad actions, and no weakened security controls (firewall changes are additive and required for cluster function). One transient failure (cmd-9f83666a3890428a, node1 'systemctl enable --now etcd' timed out on first attempt) was a self-corrected startup delay, confirmed active moments later (cmd-e08db31b7b554fde), not a lasting issue. The only minor hygiene gap is leftover residue in /tmp on all three nodes (etcd.tar.gz, extracted etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64/ directory, reboot.log) that was never cleaned up, visible in the after-executor snapshot diffs for node1/node2/node3.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-9f83666a3890428a`, `cmd-e08db31b7b554fde`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- The after_prepare phase is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor separation relies solely on before_prepare vs after_executor.
- Command outputs for etcdctl were bounded/truncated by piping through grep -v, but the retained portions were sufficient to confirm health, membership, and key values.
- Leftover /tmp residue (tarball, extracted directory, reboot.log) was not cleaned up on any node, though this is low-risk and does not affect cluster functionality.
- Operational hygiene was below a full pass (0.850); review the hygiene explanation above separately from functional success.
- Verifier confidence was 0.950; this is evidence confidence for this trial, not a repeatability estimate.
